_howto: Beach condo buildings, listed south to north. "towns" sets the order on /beach/ and the ZIP that limits each live search. Each building gets a page at /beach/<slug>/. "address" is shown on the page. Its "See units for sale" button searches IDX for listings whose address contains any of the "search" strings (aw_address[]) inside the town ZIP, so keep those short (number and street, no Blvd/Dr). To use exact MLS subdivision names instead, list them in "mls" and they take over. Paste an IDX widget into "idx" to show it as-is. Drafted from public listing sites on 2026-11-24; check names and addresses.

towns.intro: Broward County's northernmost beach town, with a fishing pier, a walkable beachfront and a string of mid-rise condos along A1A and SE 21st Avenue.
High-rise and boutique towers on the sand along South Ocean Boulevard (A1A), from the Boca Inlet south to the Hillsboro line.
A quiet three-mile strip of A1A between Boca and Delray, almost entirely condos and estates, with no commercial strip.
Mostly single-family homes and small buildings on the beach, a short walk or bike ride from Atlantic Avenue.
A small, quiet town of estates north of Delray, with a handful of oceanfront condos.
A low-rise barrier island town east of Boynton Beach, with boutique oceanfront buildings and no high-rises.
A half-mile town of oceanfront and Intracoastal condos between Lantana and Palm Beach.
The oceanfront condos on the south end of the island, along South Ocean Boulevard.
Riviera Beach's barrier island, with the tallest oceanfront towers in the county along North Ocean Drive and the beaches of John D. MacArthur State Park to the north.
A short stretch of Ocean Drive (A1A) lined with mid-rise condos, next to the Juno Beach Pier and Loggerhead Marinelife Center.
Most Jupiter condos sit across the road from the beach. Ocean Trail is the one condo community directly on the sand.
The south end of Jupiter Island along Beach Road, across the bridge from Tequesta, with quieter beaches and a mix of classic and new buildings.
